item.title: Were the Building Blocks of Life Delivered to Earth?
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
The benefits of a precious package can only be realized if an agent brings it to its destination. The wind acts as the agent delivering dandelion seeds to a fertile ground and allowing new dandelion flowers to blossom. For over a century, it has long been conjectured that comets (icebergs) or rocks (asteroids) delivered the building blocks of life to Earth. This week, a new Nature paper here argues that the rapid decline in Earth’s cometary impact bombardment at late times and the efficient destruction of fragile cometary organics at the high impact speed of comets diminish the prospects of a successful delivery of prebiotic feedstock molecules, like hydrogen cyanide (HCN), to Earth.

Below is the transcript of an interview that I had last night with Jesse Weber at NewsNation about this paper. Jesse’s questions are labeled with JW and my answers with AL. The full video clip is available here.

***

JW: What’s the origin of life on Earth? We thought we knew. Scientists for over a century believe that comets provided the seeds for life right here on Earth. The theory was that these comets were packed with the necessary carbon and nitrogen molecules to spark life on this planet but now there is a new study out of the University of Cambridge that is putting all of that into question. This study took a look at one main compound HCN which is composed of hydrogen carbon and nitrogen, and it suggests that the rate a comet travels and the angle of its impact on Earth would cause these molecules to vaporize. While the study says it’s not impossible, they say it would be statistically unlikely that HCN was delivered to Earth by comets. A comet would have to survive a fluke soft landing.

There would not be enough concentration of the molecules in water to create life.

So how exactly does this study impact our understanding about life on Earth? That’s why we got Avi Loeb, Harvard professor, astrophysicist, head of the UAP Advisory Council.

Good to see you, sir. So, what do you think? Is it very unlikely that comets are the source for life on Earth?

AL: Thanks for having me. The paper that came out last week considers, as you mentioned, just one molecule, hydrogen cyanide (HCN), which is considered to be an important critical precursor for the origin of life because it serves as a universal chemical building block for all the major components of living cells, like nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, and so forth. However, the authors find in the same paper that the delivery of hydrogen cyanide (HCN) to a planet like Mars is much more likely. The main reason that it’s destroyed during impacts on Earth is because most comets arrive at very high speed, given that Earth is closer to the Sun than Mars. And so, the molecule is destroyed in the cometary fireball that results from friction on air. But on Mars, HCN could have been preserved.

Obviously, if comets established life on Mars early enough, primitive forms of life like microbes could have been delivered to Earth through asteroids. We know that rocks rather than icebergs could survive entry through the Earth’s atmosphere if they originated on Mars.

We have some examples of rocks, like ALH84001 (as reported here) that were not heated above 40 degrees Celsius from origin on the Martian surface to delivery on Earth’s surface. If such rocks carried microbes in them that came from Mars, that could have triggered life on Earth.

JW: So, we’re Martians? We’re Martians, potentially?

AL: It’s quite possible. We don’t know that for a fact. We know that the first forms of life, the Last Universal Common Ancestor (LUCA), emerged about 4.2 billion years ago (as reported here). That is after Mars was able to cool to habitable conditions. Mars is a smaller object than Earth that provided the conditions for life earlier than Earth. We know that it had liquid water on the surface early on when LUCA showed up. So, it is quite possible that local life was triggered first over there.

JW: Is there any other explanation that, put aside an asteroid, put aside a comet, put aside that delivery mechanism, for the emergence of the building blocks of life here on Earth?

Is there another way that this could have happened?

AL: Of course, HCN could have formed out of the hydrogen, carbon and nitrogen that were available here on Earth. The authors of this paper considered comets that are thought to have delivered water to Earth. But the hydrogen cyanide molecule could potentially also exist in rocky asteroids that are not as fragile and could be delivered to Earth. I would not dismiss other channels of delivery.

The paper only shows that hydrogen cyanide has a hard time surviving when delivered in iceberg form through the atmosphere of Earth, because the comet gets vaporized and reaches very high temperatures as a result of the high impact speed.

JW: How does this impact our understanding of not only the history of our planet, but where we fit in the universe?

AL: This paper just rules out one delivery channel of one type of molecule through icebergs, but not necessarily through rocks. There could be molecules other than hydrogen cyanide that played an important role.

Incidentally, we know that hydrogen cyanide was shed by the interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, which passed through the inner solar system last year. We also know that amino acids are very common in asteroids in the inner solar system, like Bennu and Ryugu, based on studies of their material in laboratories on Earth. So, it’s possible, for example, for the building blocks of life to have been available on rocks that survived the passage through the Earth’s atmosphere. Big asteroids only get heated on their surface, but not much in the core as they pass through the Earth’s atmosphere (as reported here).

JW: Is there a way to think about this, that the authors could be wrong? The perfect conditions could have existed at that one time for that comet to come through. I hear exactly what they’re saying in terms of it vaporizing and also the severity of the impact. But it is possible that there could have been the ideal conditions in one large comet for it to happen.

AL: Indeed. For example, the authors do the statistics based on their estimated impact rate.

And they find that early on in the solar system, there was a heavy bombardment of comets, but that was too early for life to develop on Earth. One needs just the perfect object that would move along at the Earth’s orbital velocity around the Sun so that it would not impact the Earth’s atmosphere at a high speed. Who knows, maybe one such object existed? These are statistical arguments.

It’s also possible that we are all Martians. That wouldn’t be so bad. It would mean that Elon Musk is trying to deliver human beings back to Mars. But in fact, there were tiny astronauts in the form of microbes that were the first to make the trip the other way around billions of years ago. This teaches us a sense of cosmic modesty that tasks that are far more impressive than what we are trying to accomplish with our technologies were already performed by nature, billions of years ago.

JW: You know what? A lot of people who are listening to this and probably thinking: “I always felt like I didn’t belong here. Why do I feel like this planet is not right? Now I get it. I like that theory. That is a theory I have not heard yet and I am going to be thinking about that.

Professor Avi Loeb, thank you so much for always taking the time. I know your time is precious and I appreciate it.

AL: Thanks for having me.

ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Avi Loeb is chair of the UAP Science Advisory Council to the White House, Pentagon, FBI and intelligence agencies, director of the Galileo Project, founding director of Harvard University’s — Black Hole Initiative (2016–2021), former director of the Institute for Theory and Computation at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics (2005–2026), and the former chair of the astronomy department at Harvard University (2011–2020). He is a former member of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (2018–2019) and a former chair of the Board on Physics and Astronomy of the National Academies (2018–2021). He is the bestselling author of “Extraterrestrial: The First Sign of Intelligent Life Beyond Earth” and a co-author of the textbook “Life in the Cosmos”, both published in 2021. The paperback edition of his new book, titled “Interstellar”, was published in August 2024.

item.title: Will Life Exist in the Solar System After the Death of the Sun?
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
The Sun is ~4.6 billion years old. Within ~5 billion years, the hydrogen fuel in its core will run out, and the Sun will begin expanding into a red giant star. In ~6.5 billion years, the helium in its core will ignite and the Sun will settle into a helium-burning phase lasting ~100 million years. In ~7.5 billion years, the helium will be exhausted, and the Sun will enter the asymptotic giant branch, and its envelope will swell to near Earth’s orbit.

Most of the outer layers of the Sun will be shed off over a few hundred thousand years, so that in ~8 billion years the ejected gas will create an extended planetary nebula. The exposed hot core, a dense carbon-oxygen white dwarf, will carry about 0.55 solar masses. This massive remnant of the Sun will settle to a size comparable to that of the Earth.

As a result of this predictable evolution, the solar system will become a ghostly remnant of its former self once the age of the Universe will exceed 21.8 billion years. Its transformation will follow the following stages.

During the red giant phase, the Sun will engulf and completely incinerate the inner solar system. Mercury and Venus will be swallowed first. Earth will likely be engulfed as well, in which case the Moon will crash on Earth’s surface as a result of drag on the puffed-up stellar envelope. The mass loss from the Sun will initially weaken the Sun’s gravity and push Earth out to about 1.7 times the current Earth-Sun separation, namely, 1.7 AU. But the bloated Sun will also drag Earth’s orbit inward, and the most detailed models find that Earth will be pulled in and be vaporized. Even if Earth narrowly escapes being swallowed, its oceans will boil, its atmosphere will be ripped away, and its surface will melt into a sea of lava, leaving behind a scorched, lifeless rock.

The white dwarf remnant will start with a surface temperature over 100,000 degrees Kelvin and gradually cool over time. With less gravitational pull from the dead Sun, the surviving planets: Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, will drift outward. Their orbits will roughly double in size, shifting Jupiter to ~10 AU and Neptune to ~60 AU. The white dwarf’s luminosity will drop below a thousandth of the current solar luminosity within a few hundred million years. The subsurface oceans of Europa and Enceladus will eventually freeze solid. The Kuiper belt and Oort cloud will expand, and the loosely bound objects in the outer Oort cloud will be lost as interstellar objects. The changing gravity will also disrupt the asteroid belt, sending many space rocks towards interstellar space.

The white dwarf will contain no nuclear fuel and will only glow from leftover trapped heat. As it will cool down over trillions of years, the outer planets and their remaining moons will plunge into a deep freeze, with temperatures dropping down to tens of degrees above absolute zero.

Because of the chaotic shifts in gravity during the Sun’s death throes, millions of comets and asteroids from the Kuiper Belt and the Oort Cloud will fall inward toward the white dwarf. The immense gravitational tidal forces close to the dead Sun will shred these rocky objects into dust, forming a debris ring around the white dwarf that it will slowly consume over time.

Such debris disks are commonly found around old white dwarfs which represent the corpses of billions of ancient suns that died by now in the Milky-Way galaxy. The Sun was born and evolved in the last third of cosmic history. Most stars formed billions of years before the birth of the Sun.

The future solar system will lose its current inner planets, while the outer planets will survive on wider orbits around a cooling ember, and over trillions of years even that arrangement will slowly break apart.

Spectra of about a quarter to a half of white dwarfs show heavy elements in their atmospheres that gravity should have removed in days to centuries, so they must be continually fed by rocky debris. The surviving planets’ gravity, once the stabilizing mass of the star is reduced, scatters asteroids and comets onto orbits that pass close to the white dwarf, where they are shredded by tides into debris disks and accreted. Several white dwarfs show transiting fragments doing exactly this. The Solar System’s white dwarf will likely be polluted by rocky material the same way for billions of years, and its spectrum will carry the chemical signature of the asteroid belt.

With the Sun’s mass halved, the planets’ mutual perturbations are relatively stronger. Long-term simulations find the giant planets usually remain stable for tens of billions of years, but on timescales of trillions of years, passing stars and chaotic interactions will eventually eject planets one by one or send them into the star. Over such long timescales the white dwarf itself will cool dramatically and become a black dwarf, radiating almost nothing after 10 trillion years.

Interestingly, a white dwarf has a habitable zone, close in at a few hundredths of an AU, and it persists for billions of years as the star cools. No planet of the current Solar system will be there, since anything that close will be engulfed. But some white dwarfs have been found with planets that migrated inward or formed after the giant phase. If life could get a foothold on such a world, it would have a far longer stable habitable era than the Sun currently offers.

***

In this essay, I featured eight amazingly beautiful watercolors from a series created and sent to me by the celebrated artist, Greg Wyatt.

***

item.title: Will Mathematics in the Age of Superintelligence Follow the History of Astronomy in the Age of…
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
Will Mathematics in the Age of Superintelligence Follow the History of Astronomy in the Age of Instrumentation?

Ancient astronomy was practiced for thousands of years. For example, the Mayans used their eyes to track changes in the positions and relative brightness of the Sun, Moon, planets and stars for over 2,000 years. Mayan astronomers acquired the highest status in their society as priests who advised their rulers on major decisions about state events, marriages, and wars.

The human eye achieves an angular resolution of about an arcminute (1/60th of a degree) in the visible wavelength band between 380 and 720 nanometers. Given the limited collecting area of the pupil, 3–50 square millimeters, humans were able to see only relatively bright sources of visible light, as needed for their survival. Mayan astronomers with sharper eyes had the privilege of identifying fainter sources in the sky. Given the interest of Mayan rulers in their findings, they must have been celebrated and rewarded based on the quality of their eyesight.

Starting with Galileo Galilei in 1610, astronomers employed telescopes to observe the sky. 380 years after Galileo’s first observations, the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) was launched beyond the Earth’s atmosphere, to alleviate the compromising atmospheric glow and blur. HST features a primary mirror with a collecting area of 4.52 square meters, about 100,000 times bigger than a fully dilated human eye. Its angular resolution is 1,200 times sharper and it can detect sources that are 10 billion times fainter than what an unaided human eye can see.

Whereas early telescopes probed electromagnetic waves at the frequency range visible to the human eyes, their advanced successors probed other frequencies including the radio, infrared, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma-ray bands. In addition, the detection of cosmic-rays, neutrinos, and gravitational waves offered new insights on otherwise invisible processes throughout the cosmos.

Are we witnessing an accelerated repeat of this history in the context of mathematics in the age of artificial superintelligence?

Traditionally, mathematicians used their biological brains to prove or disprove research conjectures. Over the past few months, advanced reasoning models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepMind have generated thousands of pages of manuscripts, found counterexamples to long-standing math problems, and computerized historic human proofs. These include discovering a partial proof of the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis and a major special case of the Hodge Conjecture, disproving long-standing conjectures such as the Köthe Conjecture, the Ibragimov–Iosifescu Conjecture, the Discrete Geometry Conjecture, the Crouzeix Conjecture, and the Erdős Unit Distance Conjecture. Superintelligence (SI) agents successfully resolved several open Erdős problems and verified dozens of integer sequence conjectures. SI labs now pair Large Language Models with interactive proof assistants like Lean. The SI acts as the creative engine, guessing lines of a proof, and Lean acts as a fact-checker, telling the SI if a step violates mathematical rules. This feedback loop allows SI agents to autonomously debug their logic until a bulletproof code certificate is produced

The use of instruments with super-human abilities to explore mathematical truths resembles the use of astronomical instruments to explore invisible truths in the sky. In both cases, the limited biological abilities of humans are assisted by hardware to extend the human reach.

There was no way for Galileo Galilei to imagine the discovery of the galaxy GN-z11 by HST. This galaxy existed during the cosmic dawn, 400 million years after the Big Bang, when the infant Universe was only 3% of its current age. Galileo did not know that stars emit light from so far away, nor that the Sun is late to the cosmic party since it formed in the last third of cosmic history. His concept of the world included the solar system and some bright stars near it. That was it.

Similarly, traditional mathematicians used the limited neural network at their disposal in their biological brain to explore mathematical truths in the domain accessible to their brain. As of now, SI helps us resolve open questions that were defined by these same human brains. But in the future, SI could reveal new mathematical truths that the human brain did not even imagine.

Whereas the revolution in our understanding of the cosmos was brought about by centuries of improving astronomical instrumentation, the SI revolution in mathematics takes place rapidly over a period of only months. It took the Vatican 350 years after the death of Galileo to admit that he was right. But it takes Lean at most hours to check math derivations by SI.

What are humans to do under these circumstances?

Mathematicians can learn from the historical precedence of astronomy in how to adapt to emerging technologies. The proper approach is to take advantage of technological assists and change the skills necessary for making breakthroughs. The expertise needed to take advantage of HST data is very different from that employed by Mayan astronomers.

The Physics Nobel Prize was awarded in recent decades to astronomers who did not necessarily have exceptional eyesight like the Mayan astronomers, but instead had the vision to employ the latest technologies to discover the faint radio glow from the Big Bang (here and here), the existence of black holes and neutron stars in the infrared (here), X-rays (here), gravitational waves (here) and neutrinos (here and in 2026 here).

Similarly, the Fields Medal could be awarded in the future to mathematicians who discovered, with the help of SI, mathematical territories that extend well beyond the imagination of traditional mathematicians.

item.title: Is There Life in Liquid Water Now on Mars at a Depth of 5 to 10 Kilometers, and Could We Find It?
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
On Earth, deep subsurface life extends several kilometers down and may hold a comparable biomass to everything on the surface. Bacteria have been recovered from 5 kilometers deep in continental boreholes. The upper temperature limit for known life is about 122 degrees Celsius (°C).

Could the same be true of Mars? The Martian crust warms with depth at roughly 10–20 °C per kilometer. Starting from a mean surface temperature around −60 °C, the temperature ranges between about 0 and 120 °C at depths of 5 to 10 kilometers, potentially allowing life to survive in liquid water.

In 2018, the Mars Advanced Radar for Subsurface and Ionosphere Sounding (MARSIS) on ESA’s Mars Express orbiter, detected a strongly reflective patch about 1.5 kilometers beneath the south polar cap. Its initial interpretation in terms of a subglacial lake of salty water was later replaced with the understanding that it is more likely a layered volcanic rock. It was also realized that perchlorate salts found by NASA’s Phoenix and Curiosity robotic missions, can pull water vapor from the air and form liquid films at night, a process Curiosity has indirectly detected. These are thin, briny, and fleeting layers, not an aquifer.

However, in 2024 the robotic NASA lander on Mars InSight, measured seismic velocities which revealed mid-crust beneath the lander, about 11–20 kilometers down, which is best explained by fractured rock saturated with liquid water. If that holds globally, the reservoir would be enough to cover Mars with a water depth of 1–2 kilometers, which would account for much of its missing ancient water in its hypothesized ancient lakes and oceans. The supporting evidence was presented in three papers here, here and here. The inference rests on one location and on model assumptions about rock porosity, so it is not conclusive without supporting data from more stations.

The deep Earth biosphere exists without sunlight or surface organics. Its microbes use hydrogen produced when water reacts with iron-rich minerals or when radiation from radioactivity splits water molecules in a process called radiolysis. The crust of Mars is basaltic, iron-rich, and radioactive enough that models find radiolysis alone could sustain microbial populations for billions of years. A 2021 study of Martian meteorites published here, concluded their mineralogy would generate enough hydrogen to support a deep biosphere on Mars comparable to Earth’s.

If life arose on the Martian surface during its wet period of 3.7–4 billion years ago, the deep crust is the one place it could have followed the water as the surface dried. Groundwater would have been connected to surface lakes then, so no migration across dry rock was necessary. In that case, the deep aquifer is not just habitable but is the one environment on Mars that has stayed habitable continuously.

In 2022, a rose-colored, 800-gram meteorite from Mars, labeled Teghaza 001, was discovered in the Sahara Desert in Mali. Its analysis was published here a few days ago and revealed that its age is at least 4.1 billion years old. This rock is a pristine piece of Mars’ primordial crust, providing a rare “Rosetta Stone” window into the Red Planet’s deep geological past. Microscopic analysis showed the rock’s minerals were heavily altered by liquid water about 4.1 billion years ago. This indicates that early Mars had a far more active subsurface water system than previously realized. Trapped hydrogen isotopes inside the rock show that even 4.1 billion years ago, Mars was already rapidly losing its lighter elements to space, hinting that its transition to a cold, dry world began early.

How feasible is it to drill Mars down to a depth of 5 to 10 kilometers in order to reveal whether it has life right now?

The deepest hole ever made is NASA’s Perseverance rover’s sampling cores at a few centimeters. InSight’s heat-flow probe, designed to reach 5 meters down, stalled at about 40 centimeters because the soil did not give it the friction it needed. ExoMars’ Rosalind Franklin rover, now scheduled for 2028, carries a 2-meter drill.

Terrestrial rigs that reach 5 kilometers weigh hundreds of tons and run on megawatts of power, with crews on site to change bits and handle casing. The Kola Superdeep Borehole took 19 years to reach 12 kilometers on Earth, with unlimited human attention and a surface base. Deep holes need to lift the rock debris out and to stop the walls from collapsing. On Earth the drilling mud is circulated by pumps and steel casing strings. Hard basalt erodes bits. Every bit change on Earth means pulling the entire string out and running it back in, which at 5 kilometers means days of work per change. A robot on Mars would have to do this thousands of times.

A simpler approach is to let geology do the digging. Impact craters, canyon walls, and fresh landslides expose material from kilometers down. The Martian Valles Marineris cliffs reach 7 kilometers, and some crater central peaks uplift rock from 5–10 kilometers. A rover at the base of such an exposure can sample deep crust without a drill. The downside is that the rock is dry and ancient by the time it is exposed, so it reveals the deep environment’s history, not whether water and life are there now. The challenge would be to sample deep fluids as soon as they surface. If the deep aquifer ever vents through fresh impacts, volcanic regions, or seepage, surface chemistry would carry its signature. A dedicated mission to a young volcanic or impact site, offers the best prospects for unraveling subsurface life on Mars.

The simplest way to confirm the aquifer is a network of seismic stations. A permanent human base with heavy equipment, local manufacturing of casing and bits, and years of continuous operation, could eventually accomplish the required drill and unravel not only water or life but also oil (as discussed here) that could power the local technological infrastructure.

item.title: Is UAP Storytelling Akin to Religious Myths?
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
A system of statements based on conviction rather than evidence is closer to religion than it is to science. Of course, I know of many scientists who are also religious but they fully recognize the difference between scientific knowledge and religious belief.

The space of possible realities is far greater than the specific physical reality that we live in. As a result, human history is full of imagined stories. In the same vein, the practice of science is full of conjectures or unproven theoretical ideas. But what makes science different from politics or religion is the surrender to empirical evidence as an arbitrator.

The quest for evidence is commonly adopted by detectives who aim to resolve mysteries, including fictional characters like Sherlock Holmes who was quoted by Arthur Conan Doyle as saying: “When you have eliminated all which is impossible, then whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.” This assertion is certainly true about quantum mechanics as the counterintuitive nature of physical reality. The 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to Alain Aspect, John F. Clauser, and Anton Zeilinger for their groundbreaking experiments with entangled photons. Their work confirmed the reality of quantum entanglement and proved that Albert Einstein’s objections to this phenomenon, which he famously derided as “spooky action at a distance,” were incorrect.

Other scientific mysteries over the past century remain unresolved. Chief among them is the challenge of unifying quantum mechanics and gravity. The latest conjectures about doing so in the presence of extra dimensions or supersymmetry lack empirical support. This does not make these scientific ideas resemble religious myths because the physicists who explore them recognize that they can only gain traction by experimental support.

What makes the situation confusing for the general public is that most often, the scientific data necessary for drawing definitive conclusions is absent or not good enough. In politics or religion, conviction is sufficient for attracting many likes on social media because confidence is regarded as an admirable trait in our otherwise fragile life. However, in science, the most accomplished mathematicians engaged in String Theory or even the most advanced version of superintelligence, will not be able to figure out the truth about the physical reality without high-quality data from instruments that probe it.

The approach of physics is an extension of the way our body works. We rely on data from our biological sensors, known as receptors, to monitor the internal state of the body and interpret the external world. These native sensors detect physical, chemical, or mechanical changes and translate them into electrical signals that our brain can process. But the data is often insufficient for drawing definitive conclusions.

When we see a cat walking towards a building and appearing on the other side, our mind comes up with the plausible conjecture that a single cat existed throughout the entire period even though our view of the cat was blocked by the building during some of the time. Alternatively, we can imagine that there are numerous identical cats hiding behind the building with only one coming out after some time. The only way to figure whether this hypothesis is true or false is to gain a direct view of the other side of the building. This does not require that we access the other side, which might be unfeasible if obstacles block our way. Instead, we can use a drone camera or a fortuitously-positioned window that reflects the image of the hidden region.

Social-media influencers might prefer not to collect any data, because the lack of conflicting evidence gives them the license to spread the “many cats interpretation” and attract followers. The temptation to spread myths is attractive because it offers a shortcut to societal notoriety. On the other hand, the use of scientific instruments to vet the “many cats interpretation” offers us a better path forward than the number of likes a story gets.

Consider Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP), formerly known as UFOs. The fact that UFO reports persisted for 80 years does not lend credence to their alien technology interpretation. The Vatican insisted on the popular story that the Earth is at the center of the Universe for many centuries, but eventually admitted on October 31, 1992 that this story was false. Unlike blockbuster script writers in Hollywood, nature is under no obligation to follow our wishes.

Most of the time, scientists must remain agnostic because the data is not good enough to deliver a verdict about the validity of a hypothesis or an interpretation. Patience is key. The rush to a premature conclusion can have disastrous public relations consequences, as in the case of the old cosmological model of the Catholic Church.

Jay Stratton’s new book about UAP, Out of the Shadows, employs a “self-sealing” logical framework that preemptively labels skepticism as part of a government conspiracy. This rhetorical strategy creates an unfalsifiable loop where any demand for hard evidence is automatically twisted into proof of a cover-up. This type of closed epistemic system operates through several distinct layers. Testimony alone is treated as absolute truth, while the standard scientific requirement for verifiable data is reclassified as a hostile act of disinformation. Skeptics are told that if they feel genuinely unconvinced, they are simply victims of brainwashing, stripping away their critical thinking agency. By framing the debate as an ongoing war against “gatekeepers,” this narrative guarantees an endless demand for future books, documentaries, and media appearances to counter the alleged cover-up. This framing does not mean that Stratton is wrong about everything he says. He has admirable credentials as the leader of the UAP Task Force within the U.S. government. Testimony from a credible insider is a legitimate reason to investigate. But it’s a reason to start, not a reason to stop, and a book that treats its own testimony as the terminus of inquiry is overreaching. The honest reading of “we now know with certainty” is “I am certain,” which is a statement about Stratton’s mind, not about what’s in a hangar of a supposedly alien spacecraft.

On September 10, 2026, I humbly invited Jay Stratton to meet with the UAP Science Advisory Council or disclose evidence that will guide us to support his public statements. My invitation was repeated by Council member, Dr. Tim Gallaudet, but I received no response from Stratton. Instead, I was attacked personally by believers who argued: “How dare you question what Jay Stratton said? He knows what he is talking about.” I respect their conviction but this is not how science works. We must have access to evidence or else such claims do not hold water.

Paraphrasing Sherlock Holmes: “When you have eliminated all which is impossible to explain UAP, such as birds, meteors, balloons, drones, missiles, aircraft or satellites, then whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.” For now, the UAP Science Advisory Council provided evidence in a paper posted here that more than 8% of the UAP videos declassified by the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters involve birds. Regarding the identity of the remaining 92%, we have to remain agnostic and collect better data or check the hangars that whistleblowers guide us to.

item.title: Our Cosmic Archaeological Dig
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
The Universe started with nearly the same initial conditions in all directions and distances. As a result, cosmic time was nearly synchronized everywhere we look. This means that the Big-Bang instant in our past, when the density of matter and radiation diverged, occurred at the same time everywhere we look. As a result, light traversed the same distance towards us since that singular beginning from all directions. As we look out, our cosmic horizon is a spherical boundary, defined by the distance that light traversed over the past 13.8 billion years. That the initial conditions were similar out to much greater distances is a moot point because we cannot access these regions.

The Universe was transparent to gravitational waves since the earliest Planck time of its expansion history. But the thermal background of gravitons is extremely difficult to detect, as explained in my paper with Sunny Vagnozzi here.

The hot cosmic gas cooled and rarefied enough to become transparent to light about 400,000 years after the Big-Bang. The transition to electromagnetic transparency occurred as soon as free electrons were cold enough to combine with protons and make hydrogen atoms. We observe the resulting cosmic microwave background photosphere from the inside in the form of a spherical last-scattering surface surrounding us. This inside-out orientation is geometrically opposite to the outside-in orientation of the spherical photosphere of the Sun.

The light emitted by sources farther away from our location must have propagated for a longer travel time in order to reach us today. This means that we see earlier images of the Universe, the farther we look. Observational cosmology is like an archeological dig in which we uncover layers that are progressively more ancient as we dig deeper. The benefit of the finite speed of light is that we can unravel cosmic history by surveying the observable spherical volume of the Universe out to our cosmic horizon. This is possible just because the Universe had nearly the same initial conditions everywhere.

Over time, the small perturbations in the density of matter grew by gravity and ended up as collapsed objects on small spatial scales. Gravity is responsible for making the Milky-Way, inside of which stars like the Sun condensed, next to which planets like the Earth formed. About 15 million years after the Big Bang, the cosmic background radiation had room temperature. If Earth-like planets had existed at that time, they would have not needed to be close to stars in order for their surface to be warmed to habitable conditions. I discussed this in 2014 in a paper titled “The Habitable Epoch of the Universe” here, and in two follow-up papers here and here.

The gravitational growth of cosmic structures stopped in the second half of cosmic history, owing to the accelerated expansion of the Universe — triggered by dark energy. The largest cosmic structures to ever collapse are clusters of galaxies with a quadrillion times the mass of the Sun. We will never see more massive superclusters collapse. They are being torn apart by the accelerated cosmic expansion.

The first stars formed 100 million years later and their ultraviolet radiation started to break the hydrogen atoms into constituent electrons and protons. This so-called epoch of reionization transformed cosmic hydrogen back to a soup of free electrons and protons within a billion years after the Big Bang. The first stars represent our cosmic roots and the scientific version of the biblical phrase “Let there be light!”

The first two decades of my career in astrophysics (1993–2013) were dedicated to theoretically predicting the properties of the first stars and galaxies. These predictions were summarized in two textbooks, titled: “How Did the First Stars and Galaxies Form?” here and “The First Galaxies in the Universe” here. By now, the Webb telescope detected the first generation of stars and galaxies consistently with these expectations, as reviewed most recently here.

The latest Webb data shows that the star formation rate per unit cosmic volume grew steadily by orders of magnitude in the period of 0.1–1 billion years after the Big Bang. The formation of the first stars marks the transition of the Universe into complexity from the simple initial conditions that can be summarized on a single sheet of paper (in terms of the matter budget [dark matter and ordinary matter] and the statistics of the primordial density fluctuations). The first stars also started the production of Carbon, Oxygen, Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Sulphur, elements that are essential for the chemistry of life-as-we-know-it. The early Universe spent only a few minutes at the temperature suitable for nuclear fusion and this short time only resulted in light elements, like hydrogen and helium with a sprinkle of lithium.

The first stars were short-lived. After tens of millions of years, most of them exploded. The inability of hydrogen and helium to cool the primordial gas effectively led to the formation of massive stars which resulted in gamma-ray bursts when some of them collapsed to black holes. Also, mergers of their black hole remnants could be detected by future gravitational-wave observatories. Finally, the Webb telescope and its followers could keep pushing the earliest stellar explosions and galaxies on record, as we probe deeper into our cosmic archaeological dig.

***

In this essay, I featured eight amazingly beautiful watercolors from a series created and sent to me by the celebrated artist, Greg Wyatt.

***

item.title: Discovery of a Dwarf Planet Candidate in the Outer Solar System by the NSF-DOE Rubin Observatory
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
The NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory discovered a new dwarf planet candidate, named 2026 ED138, in the outer Solar System beyond the orbit of Pluto. The observational data was announced today (October 27, 2026) here by the International Astronomical Union Minor Planet Center (MPC).

If confirmed, ED138 would be among the largest and brightest bodies known in this outer Solar System. A dwarf planet is an object massive enough for its self-gravity to make it nearly spherical. Based on ED138’s distance, brightness and estimated surface reflectivity (albedo), its size is estimated to be in the range between 600 and 1500 kilometers. Icy bodies this large are expected to be round.

ED138 was first identified by Matt Holman, my colleague at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian. The related Rubin Observatory data was obtained during the run up to the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). On the evening of October 13, 2026, Holman was running data collected by Rubin earlier in 2026 through a search code he developed with Kevin Napier. The code searches through billions of detections of moving objects and compares them to identify those corresponding to the same object.

To verify the validity of the discovery, a detailed search through Rubin’s catalogs and images was subsequently initiated by Mario Jurić, a former postdoc at Harvard’s Institute for Theory & Computation that I directed for 20 years, who is currently a faculty member at the University of Washington and Rubin Solar System Lead Scientist. Jurić found 20 more observations of ED138, dating back from July 11 to March 4, 2026. In total, ED138 was observed 30 times in 20 nights. Additional archival images of ED138 all the way back to 2016, were obtained by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam), mounted on the Victor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO), a Program of NSF NOIRLab. This data allowed the Rubin team to trace more than 10 years of ED138’s orbit around the Sun.

ED138 is currently at a distance of about 46 times the Earth-Sun separation (astronomical units=au), whereas the dwarf planet Pluto has an average distance from the Sun of 40 au. This makes ED138 a trans-Neptunian object (TNO), located beyond Neptune. ED138’s orbit is tilted by 25 degrees off of the plane of the Solar System planets, suggesting that it was shifted from the ecliptic plane by Neptune’s gravitational influence.

Infrared observations, potentially by the Webb telescope, are needed to constrain the exact size of ED138 and confirm its nature as a dwarf planet. Detecting the heat emitted by the planet would provide its surface temperature and allow the inference of its emitting surface area from its measured luminosity (based on its brightness and distance). If confirmed, ED138 would join the five officially recognized dwarf planets: Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea, and Makemake.

ED138 is projected on the sky close to the plane of the Milky Way, which is crowded by numerous background stars. This coincidence projection explains why ED138 was not discovered until now. Rubin Observatory’s regular and continuous monitoring of the entire Southern Hemisphere sky, combined with powerful algorithms that sift through billions of light sources in search for small moving objects, enabled the discovery of ED138.

As Rubin will continue to image the entire Southern sky multiple times for ten years, it will likely find other new members of the solar system, as well as first-time visitors in the form of new interstellar objects like 1I/`Oumuamua, 2I/Borisov and 3I/ATLAS.

***

Context: The NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory on Cerro Pachón in Chile is a joint initiative of the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) and the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Science (DOE/SC). The U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) is an independent federal agency created by Congress in 1950 to promote the progress of science. NSF supports basic research and people to create scientific knowledge that transforms the future. The DOE’s Office of Science is the single largest supporter of basic research in the physical sciences in the United States.

item.title: Our Cosmic Roots
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
Today, I responded with answers (A) to the following questions (Q):

Q: What do you see as the most consequential uncertainty in our understanding of the first stars and galaxies, and how can observations of the early universe help distinguish between competing accounts of how the first sources of light transformed the cosmos?

A: The most exciting question is how early did the first stars form after the Big Bang. Their formation marks the transition of the Universe into complexity from the simple initial conditions that can be summarized on a single sheet of paper (in terms of the matter constituents [dark matter and ordinary matter] and the power-spectrum of primordial density fluctuations on smaller scales than were probed so far). The first stars also mark the beginning of the productions of Carbon, Oxygen, Nitrogen, Phosphorus and Sulphur, elements that are essential for the chemistry of life-as-we-know-it. They represent our cosmic roots and the scientific version of the biblical phrase “Let there be light!”

About 15 million years after the Big Bang (or equivalently, a redshift of about z=110), the cosmic background radiation had room temperature. If Earth-like planets had existed at that time, they would have not needed to be close to stars in order for their surface to be warmed to habitable conditions. The popular cosmological model predicts that the first stars form 50 million years later (redshift of z~50). But we need to check if that is indeed the case. I discussed this in 2014 in a paper titled “The Habitable Epoch of the Universe” here, and discussed the broader context in two follow-up papers here and here.

There are several observational signatures that can reveal the answer. The first stars were massive and could have resulted in gamma-ray bursts when they collapsed to black holes. Also, mergers of black holes could be detected by future gravitational-wave observatories. Finally, the Webb telescope and its followers could keep pushing the earliest galaxies on record.

Q: What are your biggest challenges right now? Is it visibility, finding the right audience, getting your books to more readers, sales, or something I haven’t thought of?

A: My research focus changed over the years from the first stars to the study of black holes and recently to the search for alien intelligence. My biggest challenge right now is to discover evidence for alien intelligence. Such a discovery will be more impactful on the future of humanity than artificial intelligence (AI) because alien intelligence is likely to reflect a much bigger database than the terrestrial information used to train AI in our data centers. Most of the real estate is beyond Earth.

We are probably not at the top of the cosmic food chain and we can learn from our most accomplished counterparts. Most of the stars formed billions of years before the Sun and it will take only of order a billion years for Voyager to cross the Milky Way disk relative to the Sun. Alien probes therefore had enough time to reach us even if they used our rocket technology from the 1970s. There are of order tens of billions of Earth-Sun analogs in the Milky-Way alone. Given so many houses in our cosmic street, common sense suggests that we are not alone and many of them had residents because similar circumstances should lead to similar outcomes. Astrobiologists focus on investing more than ten billion dollars over the next two decades in searching for the chemical fingerprints of microbes. But I say that on a blind date with a cosmic partner, we should aim high rather than low. Instead of seeking abundant and mediocre dating partners like microbes, we should search for someone more intelligent than we are. The practical benefit (as in the case of my search for a wife) is that a smarter counterpart can inspire us to do better.

Traditionally, the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI) focused on electromagnetic signals, mostly in the radio. This is equivalent to waiting for a phone call. My approach is to search for a package in our mailbox. This is the goal of the Galileo Project and the UAP Science Advisory Council under my leadership. The latest papers from these initiatives were posted this month here and here.

Think of me as a curious kid, not willing to believe in stories from the adults in the room but rather interested in finding the truth based on evidence. Life can be a self-fulfilling prophecy. Without engaging in the correct search strategy, we will never find anything.

Some people who worked in the U.S. government claim that it has an alien spacecraft in its possession. To them I say: take me to the nearest alien spacecraft!

If a functioning spacecraft is parked on Earth and I am offered a seat on it, I will be first in line to board the spacecraft on a trip to an alien world. I would have no regret leaving Earth towards the stars based on my news feed on current events in our world.

Q: When something unusual turns up in the data, what does it take for you to say it’s technological rather than natural?

A: When faced with anomalous objects, I sometimes feel like the kid in Hans-Christian Andersen’s tale being told by the adults in the room: “The Emperor has clothes but they are invisible.” For example, the first interstellar object, 1I/`Oumuamua, showed non-gravitational acceleration but no coma of outgassing around it. Comet experts now label it as a dark comet, where the cometary tail is invisible. That this is endorsed as a mainstream view demonstrates that scientists do not always follow evidence. More often, they come up with excuses why the evidence is lacking. I discussed this in the context of another example: supersymmetry, in a recent essay posted here.

Regarding the signature of alien technology: with good enough data, the distinction is straightforward. Here are two examples:

1. An interstellar object showing maneuvering towards Earth that cannot be explained by gravity or cometary outgassing. Similarly, regarding the emission of an electromagnetic signal that cannot be natural in origin. Also, if we get a high-resolution image of it, one can discern whether it looks like a natural rock or iceberg or whether it appears to look like an artificially manufactured object.

2. An Unidentified Anomalous Object (UAP) in the Earth’s atmosphere or oceans, which is documented to behave outside the performance envelopes of human-made technologies. Of course, if any such object was retrieved and is currently in possession of the U.S. government or a Corporation like Lockheed Martin, it would be straightforward to infer whether its isotopic composition implies an origin from outside the Solar System, whether the material structure was manufactured artificially or whether the object functions in ways that exceed human products by a large margin.

The Galileo Project constructed three observatories and is starting a fourth observatory with the goal of collecting data on UAP. The UAP Science Advisory Council hopes to partner with the Pentagon and bring high-quality sensors to sites where UAP are observed.

Finding residents in our cosmic neighborhood could shed light on our cosmic origins story. It started simple for the first 100 million years after the Big Bang and became much more interesting 13.8 billion years later, with many intricate details waiting to be unraveled. Pretending to be the elders in the cosmos is unreasonable. We better explore the unknown with a child’s wonder. I do not pretend to do more than that.

item.title: Comments on the Seventh Pentagon UAP File Release
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
Below is a transcript of my in-person television interview with Blake Burman in The Hill on NewsNation on October 23, 2026. The interview is also available in video format here. In what follows, Blake’s questions are marked with BB and my answers with AL.

***

BB: Joining us now, Avi Loeb. He is a professor at Harvard University, also the chair of the UAP Science Advisory Council. So nice to see you. Good day to have you here in Washington. Thanks for coming in. Let’s go back to those flying triangles. What’s your theory? What do you think?

AL: We don’t know what they are. There are two types of objects that are being spotted by the Pentagon and the intelligence community: orbs and triangles, and they are hovering over strategic assets. We need to know what they are, because if you have a down-to-earth approach, you would say they are coming from adversarial nations. It is not our government that is flying them.

We shot down a Chinese spy balloon in 2023. And when I go to the kitchen and find an ant, I get worried because there must be many more ants under the sink. For the same reason, we need to figure out these objects. We won’t be able to do it based on the data that we’re given in these UAP tranches. It’s not good enough. My hope is to partner with the Pentagon and put better sensors at the locations where these objects are found.

BB: How are government officials talking and thinking about all of this?

AL: Well, there are definitely objects that both the Pentagon and the intelligence community cannot identify. And there is even a more fundamental question, because there are some reports from people who used to work in government that perhaps there are even alien spacecraft that are being held by corporations like Lockheed Martin.

I haven’t seen any evidence for that, and the officials I speak with have not seen any evidence for that. But if it exists, my plea to whoever owns them is, please take me to the nearest alien spacecraft, because I can help you figure it out. However, it may not exist.

It’s a win-win proposition to study UAP and get better data, because we will either help national security or make the biggest discovery ever made in science.

BB: My question that I keep on asking, because a lot of this is happening over military sites, is as follows: “Is this something that our military is testing on ourselves or is it adversaries potentially testing on us?”

The head of NASA, Jared Isaacman, was on the show a couple of weeks ago. I asked him a form of that question. It was: “Is this an adversary that’s testing some next generation propulsion? It’s certainly in the realm of possible. What does your gut tell you?”

Jared Isaacman replied: “I would say I would lean towards it’s either some phenomenon that can happen. There are things that can happen just like natural phenomena that can be observed. I also think there’s a good chance that there could be a Sputnik moment that’s happening and people are testing new stealthy or next-generation type technologies.”

Where do you come down between the Sputnik moment, natural phenomena, and then maybe as some of this extraterrestrial?

AL: I’m open-minded. The good thing about being a scientist is that you don’t need to know the answer in advance. In politics, very often you need to pretend to know the answer. But in my profession, we can collect evidence that will guide us. It’s like a detective story. And my recommendation is to put sensors in those locations, get better data, and figure it out like a detective. Eventually, all of us will be on the same page. You know, there are believers, there are skeptics. I’m threading in the middle between them. Both of them don’t like my approach, because they have already decided what these objects are.

BB: As part of the files released by the Pentagon today, there is a 2002 witness account from the military officer who claimed he was present in Roswell, New Mexico in 1947, and is quoted as writing or saying: “Samples of wreckage were around the table. It was unlike any material I had ever seen in my life: pieces which resembled the metal foil, paper thin, yet extremely strong, no one was able to identify the crash debris.”

That was part of the release today. Obviously, this is the incident that has captivated so many. What say you?

AL: There are always black projects that we are not aware of, engaged in developing future technologies that you can’t find in the commercial sector. For example, when the B2 bombers were tested, a lot of people thought that they were UFOs.

The challenge is to distinguish between future technologies that are currently being developed and civilians do not know about them, and actually truly alien technology, not human in origin, which might be orders of magnitude beyond what we can accomplish right now. Obviously, if we have debris of the material, we can immediately tell. But otherwise, it’s really important to separate the two. Anything that was manufactured by U.S. sources should be known to the intelligence community and the Pentagon. So, when they say something is an unidentified object, they mean it’s not from us.

BB: Let me leave you with this, chair of the UAP Science Advisory Council. This is now the seventh release. We still don’t have a `Yes’ or `No’ that the government has some answer. Do you think we’ll ever get that?

AL: I hope so within a year or two. And I hope President Trump will have the privilege of announcing whatever we find. Stay tuned! It’s a work in progress.

BB: All right. We’ll leave it there. Avi Loeb, Professor of Science from the Department of Astronomy at Harvard University. Very nice to see you. Thanks for being back.

item.title: The Triangular UAP in the 7th Tranche of PURSUE
item.dc:creator: Avi Loeb
item.content:encoded:
The seventh tranche of declassified data on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) was released today, October 23, 2026, by the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE). In contrast to all previous tranches, this one does not include any videos.

Among its 28 PDF files, there is a historical report about findings at Skinwalker Ranch in Utah. A monthly report from March 2009 implies that Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) funded faculty from the University Nevada Las Vegas to study how ten disclosure scenarios would affect the media, politics, religion, public health and academia. Scenario 1 is a U.S. government release of declassified UAP files. The report blames a “giggle factor” for academic avoidance. File D168 includes the BAASS Project Management Plan (Dec 2008, DIA contract HHM402–08-C-0072). It asks the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) to lobby for access to “biological material of potentially non-human origin”. It also describes “contact” efforts at the ranch (“we were acted upon”) on page 20 and attaches a redacted 2002 Roswell affidavit on page 46.

The file EOP-UAP-D002 (May 1963) is a White House-level report on whether to tell the public about recovered space-vehicle fragments. Arnold Fruitkin, NASA’s chief of international relations, argued a White House statement “would scare people needlessly”. He also noted that the Department of Defense and the Air Force wanted NASA as “cover”, and he opposed going to Congress because of “the harmful debate”. It is unclear whether the discussion is in reference to familiar rocket or satellite debris, or genuine UAP.

***

The highlight of this release involves a report labeled: “DOW-UAP-D176, Triangular UAP AARO Memorandum for Record, 2026.” In 2026 federal agents saw a matte black triangular craft, about 4–5 meters wide. It climbed to 60–100 meters, hovered for 20 seconds, then dove into a canyon at fighter-jet speed. It made no sound, showed no heat source, and had no visible engines or cockpit.

The PDF file reports an interview of witnesses of UAP observations at a sensitive national security site in the western United States over two days in 2026. The All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) at the Pentagon interviewed two Federal Special Agents and incorporated a corroborating account from a third official positioned at a separate observation post.

The reporting individuals stated that a triangular object rose vertically, remained stationary, and then banked and descended into a canyon. It records their descriptions of the object’s shape, color, apparent thermal signature, perceived lack of conventional propulsion features, and absence of an associated audible signature. A subsequent ground search found no visible debris or evidence of an impact in the accessible survey area.

The three witnesses are described as experienced in operational work and familiar with observing drones and conventional aircraft. One reportedly detected the object with thermal equipment, while the others observed it visually. What makes the account interesting is the combination of reported details. The object climbed almost vertically while keeping a steady orientation, then hovered. The witnesses described no sound, and the thermal view reportedly showed no distinct hot spots or temperature differences across the object. It then banked and disappeared into a canyon in just a few seconds. Those observations do not establish the nature of the UAP and the report does not include a measured speed or raw sensor recordings. The fundamental question is whether the triangular object was manufactured in a black project of an adversarial nation or an extraterrestrial project with off-world technology.

My strategic goal as chair of the UAP Science Advisory Council (https://uapsac.com/) is to deploy new and better sensors in sites where the triangular UAP or mysterious orbs were reported by PURSUE. As we get higher quality data, we will be able to identify the nature of these mysterious objects. CHRONOLOGICAL NARRATIVE OF EVENTS:

SOURCE 1 and SOURCE 2 were positioned at the primary observation post conducting routine observation support. Weather conditions were highly favorable for both visual and electro-optical collection, with unrestricted line of sight, negligible cloud cover, and late-dusk illumination. The sun had dropped entirely below the western horizon, eliminating direct solar glare. A residual sunset gradient provided a high-contrast backdrop against the western ridge lines while the deeper valley floors and canyon cuts were rapidly falling into shadow. SOURCE 2 noted he advanced with binoculars and a handheld thermal monocular; SOURCE 1 followed seconds later. Phase I — Vertical Ascent (Duration: ~10 seconds):

Upon initial visual acquisition the unidentified craft was executing a slow, controlled, perfectly vertical ascent directly over the ridge line. The craft climbed approximately two to three hundred feet while maintaining a completely static orientation without tilting, swaying, or wobbling. The non-reflective, matte black exterior presented a continuous, featureless profile with. No propulsive apertures, rotating elements, rivets, panels, windows, canopy, cabin structures, and no protrusions or structural features were observed. The ascent occurred in absolute acoustic silence. Range to the object was bounded between approximately 1.4 and 3.2 miles west of the primary observation post by terrain cross-reference.

Phase II — Station-Keeping Hover (Duration: ~20 seconds):

Upon reaching approximately 200 to 300 feet above the ridge line, the unidentified craft instantaneously arrested all vertical motion and entered a stable hover. It remained in this station-keeping attitude for approximately twenty seconds with no observable drift or oscillation. The exterior remained uniformly featureless. No heat shimmer, vapor trail, or particulate discharge was detected. The surface did not exhibit cloaking, optical shifting or distortion, or shimmering properties, remaining matte black throughout. There was no thermal fluctuation or expansion independently of the physical profile of the craft. The transition from stable hover to high-speed horizontal flight occurred without observable acceleration ramp, gradual pitching or momentum.

Phase III — Terminal Maneuver and Loss of Contact (Duration: ~2–3 seconds):

Immediately following the hover, the unidentified craft appeared to transition from a stationary position to rapid horizontal flight. Approximated by the distance made along the ridge before visual contact was lost, the SOURCES estimated that its speed was compared to that as a military fighter jet. No instrumented speed measurement was obtained.

It executed a fluid banking turn and steep, terrain-conforming descent into the canyon with drainage similar in appearance to low-altitude terrain-masking flight. The unidentified craft did not wobble, oscillate, or drift in the wind during any part of its transit, and as it banked to follow the canyon’s path, its physical profile shifted relative to the observers. The entire horizontal transition, bank, and descent lasted approximately two to three seconds before the craft disappeared behind intervening terrain. Under banking angle, the silhouette flattened and presented as a more symmetrical isosceles triangle. Absolute acoustic silence persisted throughout the high-velocity phase. Infrared tracking was lost due to the sudden acceleration exceeding the narrow field of view of the handheld monocular; subsequent unaided visual tracking confirmed the craft’s disappearance into the canyon shadows. No impact signature, smoke, dust, or physical disturbance was observed. A ground survey of the canyon drainage conducted the following morning located no wreckage, ground scarring, or vegetation damage.
